reading.body:
Meta's Gallatin campus in Sumner County, Tennessee broke ground in 2020 and represents a $1.5 billion investment by the operator. The published specifications do not include a power capacity figure, building count, or square footage. Meta reports that operational buildings achieve LEED Gold certification and that campus electricity is matched with 100 percent renewable energy as part of the operator's net-zero commitment. A Meta-supported project is adding 530 megawatts of new renewable energy capacity to Tennessee.

The campus employs 70 or more people in operational roles and drew 1,100 skilled trade workers at peak construction. Its power demand cannot be ranked against other facilities without a published capacity figure. Tennessee has 24 mapped data center facilities and only four with published megawatt figures in the operator spec pages this site has read, totaling 12.13 megawatts across the state. Gallatin's rank among facilities with published capacity is fifth in Tennessee.

Without a published power specification, the campus cannot be quantified as a constraint on AI scaling or compared to other hyperscale sites in terms of rack density or accelerator hosting potential. The investment scale, construction timeline, and renewable energy commitments indicate capability to host significant compute load once operational, but the operator has not disclosed the magnitude.
